campus_martius.text: Floodplain of the river bend west and north of the Capitol, about 2 km long; land of the Tarquins consecrated to Mars (Livy 2.5.2); muster, voting (Saepta), games, later monuments; frequently flooded (Livy 35.9.2).

hills.text: Two summits joined by a saddle (the Intermontium). Steep cliffs to the south (Tarpeian Rock) and a long steep approach, the Clivus Capitolinus, from the Forum.
Traditional site of the first settlement of Romulus (Roma Quadrata); the Germalus is the western spur above the Velabrum; house of the aristocracy in the Late Republic.
Plebeian hill, outside the pomerium until Claudius (AD 49); the secessions of the plebs went to the Aventine or Sacred Mount (Livy 3.50, 3.54).
Elongated spur east of the Palatine, enclosed by the Servian Wall (Porta Caelimontana); said to be settled by Alba refugees (Livy 1.30).
Largest of the hills; the Servian agger runs across its east side; necropolis for the poor in the plain outside the Porta Esquilina until Maecenas' gardens in the 30s BC.
Narrow spur between Quirinal and Esquiline, crossed by the Servian agger.
Highest of the traditional seven hills; Sabine (Quirinus, Fides, Salus) settlement; north-east end the Colline Gate.

other_heights.text: Outside the Servian Wall; Gardens of Lucullus and Sallustius (late Republic).
Ridge across the Tiber, a fort of Ancus Marcius (Livy 1.33.6); military flag raised during comitia centuriata.
North of the Janiculum, outside the city; fields of the Tiber plain.

plains.note: level ground 10-15 m a.s.l. (13-20 now), 3-8 m above the Tiber, a little under 2 km wide between the Quirinal and the river, with ponds and streams (not modelled)
sources: Platner-Ashby s.v. Campus Martius (read on LacusCurtius)

ridges.note: 460 m long, 180 m wide on average, NE-SW; 'surrounded by steep cliffs on all sides except the south-east' (the Forum side is softened by the valley); saddle (Inter Duos Lucos) at about 37 m, present summits 38-39 m above the Tiber (about 44-45 a.s.l.); Tarpeian cliff at the SW corner
sources: Platner-Ashby s.v. Capitolinus Mons (read on LacusCurtius)

ridges.note: The Quirinal is a narrow irregular tongue a little over 2 km long from the Porta Collina to the Collis Latiaris, sloping off more gradually on the north and west to the Campus Martius; highest point in the Royal Gardens area; a fairly deep depression joined it to the Capitol until Trajan's excavations
sources: Platner-Ashby s.v. Quirinalis Collis (read on LacusCurtius)

ridges.note: Tongue about 700 m long, area about 24 ha, height 50-57 m (originally somewhat higher), extending south-west from the Esquiline plateau; separated from the Cispius by the valley of the Vicus Patricius and from the Quirinal by the depression of the Via Nazionale; named for its osiers
sources: Platner-Ashby s.v. Viminalis Collis (read on LacusCurtius)

ridges.note: Irregular quadrilateral, highest point 51.20 m a.s.l., about 25 acres; 'almost entirely surrounded by two marshy valleys', joined to the Esquiline (Oppius) only by the narrow ridge of the Velia (here about 30 m, the Arch of Titus ridge)
sources: Platner-Ashby s.v. Palatinus Mons (read on LacusCurtius)

ridges.note: Oppius and Cispius are the two projections of the high eastern ground (Esquiliae, the older name); well wooded at first (groves Fagutalis, Mefitis, Esquilinus, Lucinae); crest positions are the modeller's reading # unverified
Northern projection of the Esquiline (S. Maria Maggiore), parted from the Viminal by the valley of the Vicus Patricius; position # unverified
Tongue about 2 km long and 400-500 m wide stretching west from the eastern plateau, ending in two promontories (Caeliolus in the east, SS. Giovanni e Paolo in the west)
sources: Platner-Ashby s.v. Caelius Mons (read on LacusCurtius)

ridges.note: Two knobs (Aventinus Maior, Minor) with a saddle; steep towards the river and the Circus. Shape # unverified: the Platner-Ashby article could not be fetched (Aventinus_Mons.html gives 404 on LacusCurtius)
sources: Platner-Ashby s.v. Aventinus Mons (# unverified, not read)

ridges.note: Collis Hortulorum: runs west from the Porta Salaria, NNW from the Porta Pinciana to the Muro Torto and west again to the Porta Flaminia, divided from the Quirinal by the valley of the Horti Sallustiani; the substructions of the Horti Lucullani altered its contour (late Republic). Crest heights 56-62 m are modern, # unverified for 509-27 BC
sources: Platner-Ashby s.v. Pincius Mons (read on LacusCurtius)

ridges.note: Long ridge on the right bank running almost due north from opposite the Aventine, 60-70 m above the Campus Martius on average; 82 m at the Porta Aurelia (S. Pancrazio), 69 m west of S. Pietro in Montorio; the Janiculum proper is the 2 km south of S. Spirito, where the ridge comes within 100 m of the river; not continuous in the north (Vatican). Heights as quoted; crest positions are the modeller's reading # unverified
sources: Platner-Ashby s.v. Ianiculum (read on LacusCurtius, page Janiculum.html)

valleys.note: ancient floor about 10 m a.s.l. (modern 14-16); the valley centre 'was originally a swamp' (traces of man at 3.6 m, burials at 6-7 m a.s.l. in the excavations)
sources: Platner-Ashby s.v. Forum Romanum (read on LacusCurtius)

valleys.note: between the Palatine's NW slope and the Capitoline, running to the river; the Forum valley's continuation, once marshy
600 m long and 150 m wide, between Palatine and Aventine (Circus Maximus); a stream through it
sources: Platner-Ashby s.v. Circus Maximus (read on LacusCurtius)

valleys.note: Argiletum and Subura, the low ground between Capitol-Quirinal and Esquiline
the depression between Quirinal and Viminal (now the Via Nazionale); the floor rises from the Subura; levels are the modeller's reading # unverified
sources: Platner-Ashby s.v. Viminalis Collis and Quirinalis Collis (read on LacusCurtius)
Platner-Ashby s.v. Esquiliae: well wooded at first, groves Fagutalis, Mefitis, Esquilinus, Lucinae (read on LacusCurtius)
Tacitus Ann. 4.65 (the Caelian once Querquetulanus, for its oaks) # unverified, from memory
Platner-Ashby s.v. Horti Lucullani (gardens, late Republic); earlier open ground # unverified

tiber.surface_source: Platner-Ashby s.v. Campus Martius: the plain was 10-15 m a.s.l. and 3-8 m above the Tiber, so the river stood at about 5-7 m
tiber.text: River 60-90 m wide through the city, flowing north to south then west; the Tiber Island and fords at the Forum Boarium; the Pons Sublicius is the earliest crossing; floods regular (Livy 7.3.2; 24.9.6; 35.9.2). Floodplain (Campus Martius, Forum Boarium, Forum Holitorium) lay 2-6 m above normal water. Harbour at the Emporium (193 BC).

valleys.text: Marshy valley between the Capitol, Palatine, Velia and Quirinal spur, drained by the Cloaca Maxima and paved from about 600 BC; the ancient ground is 4-5 m below present level.
Low marshy ground between the Capitol, Palatine and the Forum Boarium; flooded by the Tiber until the Cloaca Maxima drained it; the Vicus Tuscus ran through it; one of the oldest market places.
Long valley between the Palatine and Aventine; site of the Circus Maximus, with the Murtia/Murcia stream.
Low district between the Viminal, Esquiline and Capitol-Forum; crowded; Argiletum road to the Forum.
